html:
Masinissa was the Berber king who changed sides in the Second Punic War to back Rome, then ruled a united Numidia, in today's Algeria, for over fifty years, from about 202 to 148 BCE.

He was the son of Gala, king of the eastern Numidians, the Massylii, and fought for Carthage in Spain. After his father died he lost the throne to rivals and to Syphax, king of the western Numidians, who had sided with Carthage. In 206 BCE Masinissa went over to Rome and joined Scipio. Together they beat Syphax in 203. At Zama in 202 BCE Masinissa's horsemen helped decide Hannibal's defeat.

Rome made him king of all Numidia. He spread farming and town life and minted coins. He also kept taking land from Carthage, sure that Rome would back him. When Carthage at last fought back in 150 BCE, Rome took it as a reason for the Third Punic War, which ended with Carthage destroyed in 146 BCE, two years after Masinissa died at about ninety. His grandson Jugurtha later fought Rome in the Jugurthine War.
sum: Masinissa was the Berber king who changed sides in the Second Punic War to back Rome, then ruled a united Numidia, in today's Algeria, for over fifty years, from about 202 to 148 BCE.
